basics.name: Tommaso Bonato
basics.label: PhD Student & Research Engineer
basics.summary: Fourth-year PhD student at ETH Zürich (SPCL) under Prof. Torsten Hoefler, researching high-performance network topologies, traffic load balancing, congestion control for large-scale AI/HPC systems. Also a part-time Research Engineer at Microsoft, shaping next-generation datacenter fabrics and representing Microsoft in the Ultra Ethernet Transport Working Group.

work.name: Microsoft (via Experis)
work.summary: Design and prototype network transport protocols for Azure's AI and HPC infrastructure as part of the Network Architecture team. Microsoft representative for Ultra Ethernet (UE) Transport Working Group, helping shape congestion control and load balancing standards. Developed proofs of concept for inter-datacenter congestion control, co-design of networking and AI workloads, and packet/flow-level load-balancing schemes. Improved and extended Microsoft's C++ htsim-based simulator.

work.name: ETH Zürich - SPCL
work.summary: Research on high-performance network topologies, traffic load balancing, congestion control for large-scale AI/HPC systems under Prof. Torsten Hoefler. Focus on datacenter networking, collective communication, and network simulation.

work.name: Amazon
work.summary: EU Transportation team: built cap recommendation systems to mitigate short-term transportation capacity shortages (est. 5M USD yearly savings). Developed LSTM model in Keras for daily recommendations using AWS services. Created automated alerts for capacity misconfigurations that caught multiple high-priority issues for Prime Day.

work.name: Imola Informatica
work.summary: Developed full-stack system using Java and JavaScript to automate retrieving and displaying information from Red Hat OpenShift with interactive graph visualization.

work.name: European Space Agency (ESA)
work.summary: Developed models and tools for analyzing data from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope (launched Dec 2021). Integrated C++ libraries from Sandia National Laboratories into Fortran codebase, achieving 4× speedup.

courses: Final thesis: Analysis of Adaptive Routing in Slingshot Interconnect (with Hewlett-Packard)
Final thesis: Time series predictions with RNNs
Exchange year at UC Santa Cruz (2016-2017)
